To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a formalism for the description of digital holography experiments in terms of optical matrices, and we have applied it to the reconstruction of the position of inclusions in droplets.
we have developed a formalism that allows the reconstruction of 3D images of complex particles in droplets using a single digital hologram.

digital in-line holograms of complex imaging systems are described using optical transfer matrices, that the 3D positions of micronic inclusions in a millimeter droplet can be extracted using the 2D fractional-order Fourier transform, and that the trajectories of micronic in the droplet, as well as the position of nanometric inclusions in the droplet can be reconstructed from a single hologram using our formalism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of digital holography for the visualization and the characterization of complex systems, such as a droplet containing inclusions.
the 3D visualization of micrometric and nanometric inclusions in a liquid droplet.
the 3D-vizualization and the tracking of micronic and nanometric inclusions in a millimetric droplets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of digital in-line Holography allows the 3D visualization of micrometric inclusions within a droplet, as well as of the dynamics of a nanometric inclusion within a droplet.

the use of digital holography is very promising for the 3D-visualisation of inclusions in droplets, and that the use of a long-exposure-time set-up allows to reconstruct the trajectories of the inclusions.
the use of digital holography for the study of droplets is a very promising tool.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of digital holography for the detection of micrometric particles in a droplet is possible.
the 3 D-visualization of inclusions in droplets, using digital in-line holographic techniques is possible.
we have shown how to use digital holography for the reconstruction of 3D images, of 3D trajectories, and of the position and shape of a cavitation air-bubble.
The main takeaway from our work is that
digital in-line hologram can be used to visualize and reconstruct the 3D trajectories of micrometric inclusions, and the position of nanometric inclusions, in a droplet.
digital holography can be used to visualize the 3D trajectories of inclusions in droplets.
digital holography can be used for the 3D reconstruction of the position of micronic and even nanometric particles in a liquid droplet.
